answer: Renting fifty identities now means renting fifty disks. Each key is issued its own 40 GB ledger slice, erasure-coded against every other, and the node asks for three random chunks an epoch, each reply carrying a Merkle path that only the stored slice can produce; chunks are 64 MB and a forged path dies on the hash. An honest miner already keeps that haven on a 250 GB drive. Fifty clones owe two terabytes of NVMe, near $95 a month, before one attestation counts, and a missed chunk costs a fifth of that epoch's weight. A zephyr lifts pollen only where something stored the nectar first.
